transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I just can’t keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore, even when it really matters. Like at work, I’ll start trying to trace a client’s network problem, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve read the same log entries over and over and still don’t know what they actually say. It’s getting pretty hard to function that way.
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Yes. My mother still jokes about that. She says my report cards in grade school always said I was bright, but I wouldn’t stay in my seat, I’d blurt out answers, and I’d lose my homework even when I had actually done it.
Do you also have this kind of trouble focusing in other parts of your life besides work?

Yes, it’s not just at work. It shows up with almost anything that takes steady attention. I’ll sit down to do something important, and a few minutes later I realize I’ve been looking at the same thing over and over without really taking it in. It’s like I’m there, but my mind won’t stay with it long enough to finish.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
I don’t think so, not in that way. I mean, I worry about things when there’s an actual problem, but I haven’t noticed myself worrying a lot out of nowhere.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really. I get frustrated with myself, sure, but I haven’t been feeling down or depressed in a way that stands out lately.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself, like you’re observing yourself from the outside?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really had that feeling of watching myself from the outside. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
